standard_prerequisites.name: The diagonal of a formal algebraic space over S is representable, a monomorphism, locally quasi-finite, locally of finite type and separated
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma lemma-diagonal-formal-algebraic-space, invoked at proof lines 3562-3563
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies every property claimed for the diagonal over Y once it is identified with the diagonal over S.

core_obligations: Let T be a scheme with a morphism T -> X x_Y X (proof line 3557).
Compute the fibre product T x_{X x_Y X} X as T x_{X x_S X} X (proof lines 3558-3561).
Apply the diagonal lemma for a formal algebraic space over S to conclude all five properties of the diagonal over Y (proof lines 3562-3563).
proof_roadmap: Test the diagonal on a scheme T (proof line 3557).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism f : X -> Y of formal algebraic spaces over a scheme S, the lemma asserts that the diagonal Delta : X -> X x_Y X is representable by schemes, a monomorphism, locally quasi-finite, locally of finite type and separated (statement lines 3548-3554). The proof computes the one thing that is not immediate: for a scheme T with a morphism T -> X x_Y X, the fibre product T x_{X x_Y X} X is identified with T x_{X x_S X} X (proof lines 3556-3561), after which the claim is the relative-to-S diagonal lemma applied to that identification (proof lines 3562-3563). The level is H2: the argument is short but contains a genuine fibre-product computation that converts the diagonal over Y into the diagonal over S, which is what makes an external citation legitimate.
